transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Kline (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (AtlasPay SRE), Priya Shah (AtlasPay Head of Payments), Marco Ruiz (AtlasPay Security), Aisha Khan (AtlasPay Integrations)

SUMMARY (auto): quick console demo focusing on tracing, mapping traces to request logs, and debugging flows. Several security questions on KMS and VPC. Action: send SOC2 and schedule POC.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Ravi our SE, we'll run through the Console tracing and request logs demo then leave plenty of time for q's.
[00:08] Jordan: Hey thanks, Jordan here, we got like 45 minutes, hoping to see how we can debug payment failures latency spikes during settlement windows.
[00:14] Priya: and also security, retention and do we need private VPC for PCI stuff.
[00:18] Ravi: yep totally, we'll cover mapping traces to request logs and KMS options near the end. Quick share of my screen?
[00:25] Maya: go for it.
[00:30] [screen share start noise]
[00:34] Ravi: ok this is the Console home, upper left you can pick your project, we'll open AtlasPay-poc, first thing we'll show is the tracing tab you can see a flame chart like UI, traces grouped by route and model call.
[00:45] Jordan: is that per-request or aggregated?
[00:48] Ravi: it's per-request initially, with the ability to roll-up aggregate histograms; each trace has a trace id that ties to request logs. so if you click a trace you'll see the full span breakdown compiled kernels, kv-cache hits, model variant fallback, that kind of metadata.
[01:05] Marco: how accurate is the model variant label? sometimes ops needs exact commit hash.
[01:10] Ravi: good q, we include model version and build id, but commit hash can be included via env metadata sent on the request, it's a customer-side header we surface. sometimes the transcription reads like commit H A S H, but it's an optional header.
[01:23] Priya: okay, show a troubleshooting workflow — say a payment request timed out.
[01:27] Ravi: sure, click errors filter at top, then pick a sample trace with error status — here we have a 'timeout' span at 1.2s during the generation step.
[01:35] [mouse click sound]
[01:38] Ravi: on the right side is correlated request logs we join by trace id, so you can see request headers, route, full prompt, token counts, and downstream service calls. this helps you see whether it was a model timeout or upstream latency.
[01:50] Jordan: do you keep full prompts? PCI might be sensitive, we need controls.
[01:55] Maya: good point retention and PII controls are in the security docs, we can mask prompts and redact fields at ingestion. we also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[02:04] Marco: do you allow disabling prompt capture entirely?
[02:07] Ravi: yes, you can disable prompt logging per-route or across the org, and we store only metadata. We'll share a config example after.
[02:16] Aisha: what about retention windows and audit logs for compliance?
[02:18] Maya: default retention for request logs is 90 days for Hosted, Dedicated can extend to configurable windows or send to your S3 via log export. Audit logs for admin actions are kept per contract.
[02:28] Priya: okay good. now the trace to logs mapping — show me a real example of root cause.
[02:33] Ravi: walk-through: here's a trace where tail latency spiked notice a repeated retry span and a model fallback to fp16 quantized variant at the 2nd attempt, that increased CPU decode time. the request logs show upstream queueing at the front-end load balancer, so the root cause is burst queueing plus fallback.
[02:52] Jordan: can we get an alert when fallback occurs? we want to triage fast.
[02:56] Ravi: yes, Console Alerts can be set on trace attributes like "model_variant!=preferred" or fallback_count>0. Alerts can connect to PagerDuty, Slack, webhook.
[03:06] Priya: is alert evaluation local or across samples? we can't flood pagerduty on a large outage.
[03:11] Ravi: you can set thresholds and group_by rules e.g., only alert if fallback_rate>1% over 5m. also suppression windows.
[03:21] [short pause]
[03:25] Jordan: show request log search — we need to filter by customer transaction id.
[03:28] Ravi: yep, top-right there's a query bar, supports free text and structured fields. example: transaction_id:TX-12345 AND status:timeout AND route:payment/submit.
[03:39] Aisha: any regex support?
[03:41] Ravi: full regex and fuzzy matching, although we recommend indexed fields for large volumes.
[03:47] Marco: how big can the retention be for request logs if we don't go Dedicated? we have to keep six months for audits.
[03:53] Maya: Hosted has tiered retention typically 90 days default, paid retention add-on available for up to a year. For longer or indefinite retention we'd recommend Dedicated + S3 export or Private deployment.
[04:04] Priya: private deployment means on-prem? and does Redwood still manage the control plane?
[04:08] Ravi: Private can be VPC-hosted with a customer-managed control plane option. We can run an appliance or a self-hosted control plane depending on your compliance. We'll include a matrix.
[04:18] Jordan: okay, show debugging a real-time stream — we want to reproduce a failing session.
[04:22] Ravi: switching to Request Logs -> Live tail, you can filter and then click 'Replay'. Replay will re-run the request against a pinned model version in a sandbox environment sanitized by default.
[04:33] Priya: how do you handle secrets and downstream webhooks during replay?
[04:36] Ravi: replay is sandboxed; we strip out outbound webhook triggers and mask secrets. We provide a secure test hook to mimic downstream systems if you opt-in.
[04:45] Jordan: what's the perf impact of capturing traces and full request logs on p99 latency?
[04:49] Ravi: negligible tracing is async and sampling-based by default. For 100% capture there's a small overhead (~1-3% extra p99), but we do heavy batching and KV cache optimizations. For mission-critical low-latency routes we recommend sampling with targeted full-capture on error traces.
[05:06] Maya: quick aside — Redwood's runtime supports prefix caching and KV cache, the trace shows cache hit rates per request which helps reduce tokens and cost.
[05:14] Jordan: can we annotate traces with internal ticket ids automatically?
[05:17] Ravi: yes via headers, e.g., X-Atlaspay-Ticket set by your front end, it surfaces in trace metadata.
[05:23] [faint crosstalk]
[05:26] Marco: security — key management: can Redwood rotate keys or do we control rotation?
[05:30] Maya: you can do both. Hosted supports customer-managed KMS where you control rotation policies; we can also integrate with HSM for Dedicated/Private.
[05:40] Marco: do you provide attestation for the HSM?
[05:43] Ravi: yes for enterprise tier we provide attestation reports and can include HSM vendor details in the contract.
[05:50] Priya: latency SLOs — what SLOs do you offer for Dedicated?
[05:54] Ravi: Dedicated comes with SLOs in the contract; typical offering is p95 <200ms for small prompt generations depending on model, we can tune hardware and quantization profile for your workload. We'll capture your prompt distribution during the POC to recommend quantization.
[06:09] Jordan: speaking of quantization, we saw differences in hallucination rates. how do you evaluate quality when recommending q4 vs q2 quant profiles?
[06:16] Ravi: Redwood Optimize runs sample eval sets against variants and reports quality delta vs latency/cost. We can run those evals with your prompts in the POC.
[06:24] Aisha: show me an example of an error analysis flow end-to-end.
[06:27] Ravi: sure pick an error group, here's one with high error rate. Console shows top failing prompts, then you can open the trace that includes generation tokens and model logits snapshot (if enabled) to see if token truncation or decoding errors.
[06:40] Jordan: logits snapshot? will that be a lot of data?
[06:42] Ravi: it's optional, we stream an aggregated histogram by default to avoid large payloads; full logits snapshot is an enterprise opt-in for deep debugging.
[06:51] Priya: what about PII in those snapshots?
[06:54] Ravi: redaction and masking applies; full snapshots require a signed agreement and limited retention.
[06:59] Maya: I'm going to flip to a recent incident we annotated — this was during your 3pm settlement window last week, Jordan?
[07:06] Jordan: yep that was during batch settle.
[07:08] [screen switches]
[07:10] Ravi: so here's the incident trace: you can see two spikes, first spike queued at the ingress, second spike was a model fallback that increased decode time. Request logs show queuing due to socket saturation on the front-end nodes.
[07:22] Jordan: so cause was infra not model?
[07:24] Ravi: primarily infra. There was also an adaptive retry that caused increased downstream load you can see retry_count in the request log.
[07:31] Priya: could Redwood's autoscaler have prevented that?
[07:34] Ravi: autoscaling is configurable; for Dedicated you can provision burst capacity and tune cold-start thresholds. For hosted we have autoscale but for sustained high peaks we recommend Dedicated or pre-warmed pools.
[07:47] Marco: legal wants to know if we can demonstrate encryption in transit and at rest for this POC.
[07:51] Maya: yes TLS in transit is standard; at-rest encryption can be customer-managed KMS. We'll send the security whitepaper that includes cipher suites, KMS integration, and SOC 2 attestations.
[07:59] Jordan: okay, now how do we run a replay against a canary model to test fixes?
[08:04] Ravi: open the replay modal, choose the trace, select the pinned model version or a canary tag there's a toggle to sandbox replay vs production call. Sandbox does not hit billing or external webhooks.
[08:17] Priya: can the replay simulate the same request concurrency as the incident?
[08:21] Ravi: we have a load generator option within POC kit that replays a set of traces at specified qps. It's part of the POC plan.
[08:29] Jordan: show the logs export options — we prefer S3 shipping for retention and to run our own long-term analytics.
[08:34] Ravi: request logs can export to S3, BigQuery, or push to your data lake via connector. Exports are encrypted and can be signed with your KMS.
[08:44] Aisha: is export real-time? we need near-real-time for our fraud detection.
[08:48] Ravi: near-real-time with small buffer usually under 30s for streamed exports, depending on volume.
[08:56] [short pause]
[09:00] Maya: quick check-in — are we aligned that the big asks are PII controls, KMS/HSM details, and a POC to validate tail latency?
[09:07] Priya: yes and pricing for retention and Dedicated options.
[09:10] Jordan: plus alerting rules and replay load test.
[09:13] Maya: great. I'll drop those items into next steps after the call.
[09:18] Marco: one question on RBAC — can we limit who can see full prompts?
[09:22] Ravi: yes, RBAC per route and per role, you can restrict prompt view to certain roles; we also support SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[09:31] Priya: any audit logs for who viewed what?
[09:34] Ravi: yes, audit logs include user actions like 'view_prompt' with timestamp and user id, and they can be exported.
[09:41] Jordan: can you show a sample query we can use to find all requests that used the deprecated model variant?
[09:46] Ravi: sure model_variant:"redwood-gptx-1-deprecated" AND status:success OR status:timeout and you can add time range and host filters.
[09:56] Aisha: will that run across all regions? we have traffic in us-east and eu-west.
[09:59] Ravi: yes Console supports cross-region queries and you can filter by region; for cross-region correlation we surface timestamps in UTC and then region tag.
[10:09] Priya: any mention of cost when doing 100% trace capture during a POC?
[10:12] Maya: for POC we usually cover a baseline of capture and include guidance on the incremental cost; we'll provide a cost model based on your QPS and retention needs.
[10:21] Jordan: ok let's talk about the POC scope — we want to run a 7-day spike test with 3 hours daily ramp to simulate settlement window at 2k qps. can Redwood support that?
[10:30] Ravi: yes, we can do that with Dedicated pre-warmed pool or Hosted with committed burst. We'll propose both options in the POC plan.
[10:38] Priya: timeline for POC setup?
[10:40] Maya: typically 1-2 weeks to provision credentials, export sample data, and spin up the environment; let's aim for week of 2027-01-11.
[10:49] Jordan: agreed.
[10:51] [short pause]
[10:55] Marco: legal question — when we do replay, is there any risk of sending PHI/PPI externally?
[10:59] Ravi: replay sanitizes and we can do a dry-run which masks any PHI; full unmasked replay would require an NDA clause and limited access.
[11:08] Aisha: can you auto-sanitize certain JSON fields? e.g., card_number or ssn?
[11:12] Ravi: yes you can provide a schema or regex list to redact at ingestion.
[11:17] Priya: ok sounds good.
[11:19] Maya: I'm going to pull up a sample exported trace file so you can see the JSON structure we send to S3.
[11:25] [file download noise]
[11:28] Ravi: the file includes top-level trace_id, timestamps, spans array (start/duration/type), request_meta, response_meta, and references to model_version and quant_profile. we avoid embedding full large blobs unless enabled.
[11:41] Jordan: if we enable full logits, is that included in the same object?
[11:44] Ravi: it's attached as a separate artifact and only included if you opt-in.
[11:49] Priya: okay, any gotchas we should be aware of?
[11:52] Ravi: think about sampling on high-volume routes, index fields to speed queries, and offloading long-term retention to S3 if you want custom analytics.
[12:02] Maya: quick recap: we'll send SOC2 and KMS/HSM whitepaper, pricing/POC plan, and sample export schema. Ravi will share an example trace and a sample alert rule. Jordan will provide traffic profile.
[12:15] Jordan: I'll get the CSV with qps and percentiles.
[12:18] Priya: legal will need the attestation docs — Marco will follow up.
[12:22] Marco: yep.
[12:24] Maya: any final q's?
[12:27] Aisha: one more — for the replay sandbox can we connect to our staging service for end-to-end acceptance testing?
[12:32] Ravi: yes via secure proxy and allowlist; needs a one-time setup during POC.
[12:36] Jordan: great. thanks everyone.
[12:39] Maya: thanks folks we'll follow up with notes and next steps.
[12:42] [call end]
